note: Reads the 16-byte GUID from the ASF file to identify the object type. The GUID determines which decoder function is called next.
If the GUID matches the Codec_List object GUID (86D15240-311D-11D0-A3A4-00A0C90348F6), the codecList() function is invoked to parse the codec entries.
Reads a 4-byte little-endian DWORD from the file specifying the number of codec entries. This value is attacker-controlled and determines the loop iteration count.
Reads a 2-byte WORD from the file and multiplies by 2 to get the codec name length in bytes. The attacker controls this value; a value of 1 yields codec_name_length=2.
Calls readStringWcharTag with the attacker-controlled codec_name_length=2. This propagates the length value into the vulnerable helper function.
Checks that the requested length (2) does not exceed the remaining file size. The check passes because the file contains enough bytes.
Allocates a heap buffer of length+1 = 3 bytes. This is the buffer that will be over-read.
Reads exactly 2 bytes into the 3-byte buffer. The third byte remains uninitialized.

Constructs a std::wstring from the byte range [begin, end) which spans 3 bytes. The wstring constructor reads sizeof(wchar_t)=8 bytes at a time on this platform. Since 3 bytes is not a multiple of 8, the final read of 8 bytes extends past the 3-byte heap buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ of 8 bytes.

The over-read has already occurred during wstring construction. The corrupted wstring is then converted to UTF-8, but the memory-safety violation (heap-buffer-overflow READ 8) has already been triggered at step 9.
